extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students studying functional analysis/operator theory
extracted.subtask_description: Solve and prove the sequence of advanced functional-analysis exercises (duality map, convexity, monotone operators, Lp spaces, Radon measures, projections, etc.) appearing as textbook problems. Each numbered subquestion asks for a specific proposition or construction to prove or check under given assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundedness of M defined by level set
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f ∈ E* and α ∈ R the set M = {g ∈ E*; φ*(f − g) + ψ*(g) ≤ α} is bounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use assumption (H) and Corollary 2.5.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundedness transfer for sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Let α ∈ R and (fn),(gn) in E* with (fn) bounded and φ*(fn − gn) + ψ*(gn) ≤ α. Prove that (gn) is bounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower semicontinuity of θ
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that θ is l.s.c. (lower semicontinuous) from the previous properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove properties (i),(ii),(iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove assertions (i), (ii), and (iii) referenced earlier (compare with Exercise 1.23 question 3 and Theorem 1.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duality map derivative limit (A1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For strictly convex E* (so F(x) single-valued) check that lim_{λ→0} (1/(2λ))((||x+λy||^2−||x||^2)) = ⟨F x, y⟩ for all x,y ∈ E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Apply result of Exercise 1.25; treat λ>0 and λ<0 separately.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity at t=0 of inner product map (A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that for every x,y ∈ E the map t ↦ ⟨F(x+ty), y⟩ is continuous at t=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use inequality 1/2 (||v||^2 − ||u||^2) ≥ ⟨F u, v − u⟩ with u = x+ty and v = x+λy.]

rubrics_metrics.name: F continuous strong→weak (A3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that F is continuous from E (strong topology) into E* (weak topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use result of Exercise 3.11; also prove directly when E is reflexive or separable.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratic identity for F (A4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that ⟨F x + F y, x + y⟩ + ⟨F x − F y, x − y⟩ = 2(||x||^2 + ||y||^2) for all x,y ∈ E and deduce norm/inner-product inequalities for unit vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijectivity and inverse of F when E reflexive/strictly convex (A5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume E reflexive and strictly convex; prove F is bijective from E onto E* and that F^{-1} coincides with the duality map of E*.

rubrics_metrics.name: F strong→strong continuity under uniform convexity (B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume E* uniformly convex; prove that F is continuous from E strong into E* strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform continuity of F on bounded sets (B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that F is uniformly continuous on bounded sets of E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Argue by contradiction and apply question A4.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiability of 1/2||·||^2 and identification of gradient (B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that φ(x)=1/2||x||^2 is F-differentiable, i.e., ||·||^2 is differentiable and its differential equals F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make precise the limit: limit_{x→x0} (φ(x)-φ(x0)-⟨F x0, x-x0⟩)/||x-x0|| = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform convexity ⇔ F single-valued and uniformly continuous on bounded sets (B converse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversely, assume F(x) is single-valued for each x and F is uniformly continuous on bounded sets; prove that E* is uniformly convex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequality for conjugates and sup formula (C hint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove inequality ||f+g|| ≤ 1/2||f||^2 + 1/2||g||^2 − ⟨f−g,y⟩ + sup_{||x||≤1} {φ(x+y)+φ(x−y)} for appropriate φ,f,g,y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint included in text; used to derive other parts.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of minimizer for x↦(1/2)||f||^2 + φ*(f) − ⟨f,x⟩ (14A1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each fixed x ∈ E, consider x^: f↦(1/2)||f||^2 + φ*(f) − ⟨f,x⟩ on E*; check there exists unique f_x ∈ E* attaining the infimum and set Sx = f_x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of S : E→E* (14A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove S: x↦Sx is continuous from E strong into E* strong (first show strong→weak continuity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inf-convolution ψ properties and identification of differential (14B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ψ(x)=inf_y { (1/2)||x−y||^2 + φ(y) }; check ψ is convex, differentiable, and its differential coincides with S. Also show ψ(x) = −min_{f∈E*} (1/2||f||^2 + φ*(f) − ⟨f,x⟩) and ψ*(f)=1/2||f||^2 + φ*(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Apply Theorem 1.12.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequalities relating ψ and S (14B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce ψ(x)+ψ*(Sx)=⟨Sx,x⟩ and |ψ(y)−ψ(x)−⟨Sx,y−x⟩| ≤ ||Sy − Sx||·||y−x|| for all x,y ∈ E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction ϕ_n by Moreau regularization (14C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For n≥1 define ϕ_n(x)=inf_y { (n/2)||x−y||^2 + φ(y) } and prove ϕ_n convex,differentiable and ϕ_n(x)↑φ(x) as n→∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use same method as Exercise 1.24.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Center (Chebyshev) of a bounded set existence/uniqueness (15A1-A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given uniformly convex Banach space E and nonempty closed convex C and bounded A⊂C, define ϕ(x)=sup_{y∈A} ||x−y||. Show ϕ convex and Lipschitz; prove there exists unique c∈C minimizing ϕ (center σ(A)). If A not a singleton, show ϕ(σ(A)) < diam A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic center of a bounded sequence (15B1-B4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For bounded sequence (a_n) in C define A_n=⋃_{i≥n}{a_i}, ϕ_n(x)=sup_{y∈A_n}||x−y|| and ϕ(x)=lim_n ϕ_n(x). Prove limit exists, ϕ convex/continuous, there is unique σ (asymptotic center) minimizing ϕ, σ_n = σ(A_n) satisfy lim ϕ_n(σ_n)=ϕ(σ) and σ_n→σ strongly (use contradiction + Ex.3.29).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also determine asymptotic center if a_n→a strongly and compute in Hilbert space when a_n⇀a weakly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed point of contraction via asymptotic center (15C1-C2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T:C→C is contraction and sequence a_n=T^n a is bounded with asymptotic center σ, prove σ is fixed point of T, and the fixed point set of T is closed and convex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property (P) implies D(A) dense (16A1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A: D(A)⊂E→E* linear with monotonicity (M): ⟨Au,u⟩≥0 ∀u∈D(A). If property (P) holds (if x,f with ⟨Au − f,u−x⟩≥0 ∀u then x∈D(A),Ax=f), prove D(A) is dense in E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property (P) implies A closed (16A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that if (P) holds then A is closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convexity of u↦⟨Au,u⟩ on D(A) (16A3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove u∈D(A) ↦ ⟨Au,u⟩ is convex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel inclusion N(A) ⊂ R(A)⊥ and consequences (16A4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove N(A) ⊂ R(A)⊥ and deduce N(A) ⊂ N(A*) if D(A) dense.

rubrics_metrics.name: (P) holds when D(A)=E (16A5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that if D(A)=E then property (P) holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: (M*) for adjoint domain elements from (P) (16B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under reflexivity and strict convexity and (P), prove ⟨A* v, v⟩ ≥ 0 for all v∈D(A)∩D(A*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of (M*) to D(A*) (16B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v∈D(A*) with v∉D(A). Prove ∀f∈E* ∃u∈D(A) with ⟨Au − f, u − v⟩ < 0; choosing f=−A*v deduce ⟨A*v,v⟩>0 and hence (M*) holds on D(A*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of nullspaces and ranges for A and A* (16B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove N(A)=N(A*) and R(A)=R(A*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph norm reflexivity and convex minimizer existence (16C1-C3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming (M*), check D(A) with graph norm is reflexive; for given x,f define ϕ(u)=1/2||Au−f||^2 +1/2||u−x||^2 + ⟨Au−f,u−x⟩, show ϕ convex/continuous, coercive, deduce minimizer u0 and derive the equation relating A and A* by variational trick letting t→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Apply Problem 13, part A.]

rubrics_metrics.name: (M*) ⇒ (P) and dual property (16C4-C5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove (M*) implies (P) and deduce A* also satisfies (P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of support function ϕ for convex C (17A1-A3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M closed linear subspace and C convex subset of E*. Define ϕ(u)=sup_{g∈C} ⟨g,u⟩. Prove: for f∈M^⊥+C we have ϕ(u) ≥ ⟨f,u⟩ ∀u∈M; conversely if ϕ(u) ≥ ⟨f,u⟩ ∀u∈M then f∈M^⊥+C; and if C closed/bounded then M^⊥+C closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use Hahn–Banach for converse.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Lp example determination of M^⊥ and decomposition (17B1-B5)
rubrics_metrics.description: In E=L^p with specified M and C, check M closed and C convex,closed,bounded; determine M^⊥ and ϕ(u) for u∈Lp; deduce decomposition f=λ j + g for f satisfying integral inequality and conversely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of ϕ∈M^⊥ between f and g equivalent condition (17C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For M⊂L1 and f,g∈L∞ with f≤g a.e., prove equivalence: (i) ∃ϕ∈M^⊥ with f≤ϕ≤g a.e., and (ii) (f u+ − g u−) ≤ 0 ∀u∈M, with u± as positive/negative parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: construct ψ with |ψ|≤g−f and use Theorem I.12.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong convergence of g(un) under weak convergence and energy bounds (18 main)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let g:R→R continuous nondecreasing with growth bounds; if u_n⇀u in L^p and lim sup ∫G(u_n) ≤ ∫G(u) prove: (1) g(u_n)→g(u) strongly in L^q for every q∈[1,p^*), and (2) if g strictly increasing then u_n→u strongly in L^q for q∈[1,p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence of substeps: inequality G(a)-G(b)-g(b)(a-b)≥0, and analysis of pointwise subsequences and Fatou-type arguments; see steps 2–6 in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong convergence under additional coercivity (18 steps 7-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming |g(t)| ≥ α|t|^{p−1} − C, prove g(u_n)→g(u) strongly in L^p; discuss necessity of assumption and show strict monotonicity gives u_n→u strongly in L^p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banach space E = L1∩L2 is Banach and linear functional continuity (19.1-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check E with norm ||u||_E=||u||_1+||u||_2 is Banach; for f=f1+f2 with f1∈L∞ and f2∈L2, show u↦∫ f u is continuous linear functional on E; and continuity of weighted integral u↦∫ |x|^{−α} u(x) dx for 0<α<1/2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: split integral into |x|>M and ≤M parts.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed convex set K and weak limit preservation (19.3-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define K={u∈E; u≥0 a.e., ∫ u ≤1}. Check K closed convex; if u_n∈K and u_n⇀u weakly in L^2, prove u∈K and convergence of weighted integrals ∫|x|^{−α} u_n→∫|x|^{−α} u.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coercivity and attainment of infimum for J on K (19.5-7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define J(u)=∫u^2 − ∫(1/|x|^α) u; prove J bounded below on K, inf m achieved: show minimizing sequence bounded in E, subsequence weak limit u with J(u)=m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflexivity of E? (19.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Question: Is E reflexive? Determine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarkson inequalities and uniform convexity of L^p (20A-C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish Clarkson inequalities: for 2≤p<∞ prove inequality (1) and (2) for real numbers and deduce function f(x) properties leading to (1); extend to functions in L^p to prove Clarkson's first & second inequalities and deduce uniform convexity for 1<p<∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: use convexity and duality; refer to Exercises 4.11 and 4.10.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution function α(t) properties and representation (21A-B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given measurable f define α(t)=|{ |f|>t }|. Prove α nonincreasing and right-continuous; for fn→f a.e. prove inequalities between α_n and α and deduce α_n(t)→α(t) a.e.; for G(t)=∫_0^t g(s) ds prove ∫ G(|f|) dμ = ∫_0^∞ α(t) g(t) dt and related identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: use Fubini/Tonelli.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Lp characterization from distribution function (21B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show f∈L^p ⇔ ∫_0^∞ α(t) t^{p−1} dt < ∞ and provide the identity for ∫ |f|^p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marcinkiewicz (weak-Lp) space properties (21C1-C7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define [f]_p = sup_{A} |A|^{-1/p} ∫_A |f| and M^p; show linearity and norm property, embeddings L^p⊂M^p with bound, completeness, rephrasing via sup t^p α(t), converse inequalities with constant C_p, embeddings M^p⊂L^q for q<p, interpolation inequalities and example f(x)=|x|^{-N/p} in unit ball lies in M^p but not L^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: use B3 and decomposition of integrals; use distribution function results.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpolation theorem for linear operator T on L^p (22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T bounded L^1→L^1 and T(L^∞)⊂L^∞; with norms N1,N∞ prove T bounded on L^p for 1<p<∞ and estimate N_p ≤ 2 N_1^{1/p} N_∞^{1−1/p} (simplified case N_∞=1 provided); use truncation u=v_λ+w_λ and distribution function estimates to conclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: compute norms of g_λ,h_λ and use Problem 21 B results.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Equi-integrability equivalence with weakly compact containment (23 main)
rubrics_metrics.description: For F⊂L^1 on σ-finite measure space, prove equivalence: (i) F contained in a weakly (σ(L^1,L^∞)) compact set of L^1, (ii) F equi-integrable (properties a,b,c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break into (i)⇒(ii) using Baire category & Eberlein–Šmulian and (ii)⇒(i) via approximation by weakly compact sets; see parts A and B and hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications of Dunford–Pettis and equi-integrability (23C-D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove consequences: if f_n⇀f and a.e. convergence then ||f_n−f||_1→0; compactness of K={f:u1≤f≤u2}; every equi-integrable sequence has weakly convergent subsequence in σ(L^1,L^∞); characterize equi-integrability via convex increasing G with lim_{t→∞}G(t)/t=∞ and uniform bound ∫G(|f|)≤C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: use truncations, Problem 18, Egorov, distribution function arguments.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Separable density and approximation in C(K) (24A1-A5)
rubrics_metrics.description: On compact metric K prove C(K) separable by constructing partitions of unity subordinate to finite coverings and finite-dimensional approximations ˜f(x)=∑f(a_j) θ_j; show sup norm control and density of span of θ_j.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation of Radon measures by L^1 and smooth compact-supported functions (24B1-B5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For bounded open Ω⊂R^N identify L^1 with subspace of M(Ω); given μ0∈M(Ω) construct sequence u_n∈C_c^∞(Ω) with ∫ u_n f → ⟨μ0,f⟩ ∀f∈C(Ω) and ||u_n||_1 → ||μ0||_M. Also produce nonnegative approximations preserving mass when μ0≥0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: use weak-* density, Hahn–Banach, Corollary 4.23, normalization.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of finite atomic measures D in M(K) (24C1-C4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let D be finite linear combinations of Dirac masses. Show D is dense in M(K) for weak-* topology and given μ0 construct sequence ν_n∈D with ν_n⇀μ0 and ||ν_n||=||μ0||; for probability μ0 get ν_n probability measures approximating μ0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: same techniques as B; Krein–Milman alternative discussed.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Jordan decomposition of measures (24D1-D4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given μ∈M(K) define L(f) and μ_1(f)=L(f^+)-L(f^−); prove μ_1,μ_2=μ_1−μ are nonnegative measures with norms adding to ||μ|| and uniqueness/ordering properties of decomposition μ=μ_1−μ_2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of results to C_0(Ω) dual (24E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show results (except B6) remain valid when E=C_0(Ω) (functions vanishing on boundary), with dual often denoted M(Ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dunford–Pettis revisited: subsequence extraction to obtain weak limit in L^1 (24F1-F6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given equi-integrable sequence f_n in L^1, show existence of subsequence f_{n_j} such that f_{n_j}⇀f in σ(L^1,L^∞), via truncations T_k and weak-* limits in M and then identify limit as L^1 function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: use truncation bounds, weak-* compactness, approximation in L^∞, Egorov, and Cauchy arguments in L^1.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Projections on Hilbert spaces: cone geometry and supporting functionals (25 parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let H Hilbert, C nonempty open convex cone with 0∉C and C≠H. Define C^∘ = {u∈H; (u,v)≤0 ∀v∈C}. Prove C^∘ is nontrivial closed convex cone and represent C and C^∘\{0} via polar relations; construct bounded closed convex K subset of C^∘ with (u,ω)=−1, show K nonempty and 0∉K, find a=PK 0 ∈ (−C)∩C^∘, and deduce existence of separating point w0 for open convex D and x0∉D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: use Hahn–Banach and geometric ball in C.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Prox map existence, uniqueness, and properties (26.1-8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let H Hilbert and ϕ convex l.s.c. proper. For each f∈H prove existence/uniqueness of minimizer u solving (P) 1/2||f−u||^2 + ϕ(u) = inf; show equivalence with variational inequality (Q), Lipschitz dependence |u−ū|≤|f−f̄|, analyze special case ϕ=I_K, conjugate problem and relation u+u^*=f and I+I^*=1/2||f||^2, behavior u_λ for λ→0 (projection on D(ϕ)) and λ→∞ (projection on minimizers K), and asymptotic scaling lim_{λ→∞} (1/λ) u_λ = −P_{D(ϕ^*)}0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: coercivity, reflexivity, variational derivative, apply problem 13 A results.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate projections convergence to nearest vector (27A1-A8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two nonempty closed convex sets K1,K2 and alternating projections u_{n+1}=P2 P1 u_n etc., prove sequence (u_{2n}−u_{2n−1}) converges to z=P_{K2−K1}0 with limit norm equal to dist(K1,K2); if z∈K2−K1 (e.g., one set bounded) show subsequences u_{2n}⇀a2, u_{2n−1}⇀a1 with a2−a1=z, and apply Opial's lemma to conclude weak convergence properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hints: monotonicity of distances, inequality chains, construction in H×H and weak-closedness property (P).]

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of projections and orthogonal projections (28A-B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For linear operator P with P^2=P list equivalent properties for being orthogonal projection: P^*=P, ||P||≤1, N(P)⊥N(I−P). For involution T with T^*=T and T^2=I show (I−T)/2 is orthogonal projection and converses; for P=PM and Q=PN prove PQ=QP iff PQ is a projection, and in that case describe P Q as orthogonal projection onto M∩N and P+Q−PQ onto M+N.
